topic.subject: science
topic.title: Getting to know plants
topic.scope: herbs, shrubs, trees, stem, leaf, root, venation, flower parts, functions of each part

misconceptions.statement: All plants with thin green stems are herbs.
misconceptions.why: Students often use stem thickness as the only criteria, ignoring the height or branching pattern.
misconceptions.fix: Herbs are small plants with delicate stems, while shrubs are medium-sized with branches starting near the base.

probe.question: Is a rose plant a herb?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because it has a thin stem.

misconceptions.statement: Trees are just very old shrubs.
misconceptions.why: Students conflate the life cycle of a plant with its structural classification.
misconceptions.fix: Trees are distinct because they have a thick, hard, woody trunk with branches high above the ground.

probe.question: Does a shrub eventually turn into a tree as it grows older?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, if you let it grow for many years it becomes a tree.

misconceptions.statement: Roots are only for holding the plant in the soil.
misconceptions.why: The visible function of anchorage is obvious, while absorption is invisible and abstract.
misconceptions.fix: Roots also absorb water and minerals from the soil, which are essential for the plant's survival.

probe.question: What happens if you cut off all the roots of a plant but keep it standing in soil?
probe.wrong_answer: It will stay healthy because it is still standing in the soil.

misconceptions.statement: All plants have the same type of roots.
misconceptions.why: Students rarely observe the underground parts of different plants, assuming uniformity.
misconceptions.fix: Plants have different root systems, such as taproots with a main root and fibrous roots with many thin roots.

probe.question: Do grass and a mango tree have the same kind of roots?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, all plants have the same type of roots under the ground.

misconceptions.statement: Veins in a leaf are for carrying food to the leaf.
misconceptions.why: Students often confuse the function of plant veins with human blood vessels.
misconceptions.fix: Veins provide support to the leaf and act as channels for water and dissolved minerals.

probe.question: What is the purpose of the lines on a leaf?
probe.wrong_answer: They carry food from the soil to the leaf.

misconceptions.statement: Flowers are only for decoration and smell.
misconceptions.why: Students focus on the aesthetic and sensory appeal of flowers rather than their biological role.
misconceptions.fix: Flowers are the reproductive parts of the plant that help in producing seeds.

probe.question: Why do plants have flowers?
probe.wrong_answer: To look beautiful and smell nice for us.
